subject_entity.notes: Bishop Demetrius of Alexandria convened two synods c. 231–232 condemning Origen's irregular ordination in Caesarea and expelling him from the Alexandrian church; Origen relocated permanently to Caesarea where he continued teaching and writing for over twenty years.

object_entity.notes: Major Egyptian port city; intellectual and commercial center; seat of the Catechetical School; major Christian center from the first century onward.

evidence.notes: Eusebius records the expulsion from Alexandria.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: Origen's fame spread throughout the whole world; Beryllus of Bostra, Alexander of Jerusalem, and many other bishops invited him to teach and dispute with heretics; in Caesarea he was ordained presbyter by the bishops of Palestine, which provoked the jealousy of Demetrius of Alexandria.
passage.notes: Eusebius on Origen's fame, ordination controversy, and network of episcopal supporters
